subject: Geo-commitment, DPA redlines, and operational evidence request
messages:
From: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@healthlyte.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial ask: geo commitments + subprocessor roster

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

Following our procurement checklist: before legal signs the DPA we need a formal statement of regional processing commitments (US/EU/APAC), the current subprocessor roster, and an ops runbook that explains transient cross-region processing windows and what triggers them. Specifically Healthlyte needs: 1) Affirmation of region pinning for customer-data by default, 2) Maximum allowed transient cross-region processing window, 3) Notification SLA when a transient window will cause egress outside the customer region, and 4) any KMS/escrow options if keys must be shared for ephemeral failover.

We’ve attached our procurement questionnaire and will attach a marked-up DPA if helpful (see attached). Can you confirm what evidence you can provide (audit log snippets, subprocessor activation timestamps, example alert emails)? We’re on a tight timeline to close this week if possible.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellison
Director, DataOps | Healthlyte
attachments: Healthlyte_procurement_checklist.xlsx
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@healthlyte.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask: geo commitments + subprocessor roster

Tom — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the items you asked for; below is a short plan and the questions we need answered to finalize the MAP and the evidence bundle.

Summary of what Redwood can commit today:
- Default region pinning: customer data is routed and stored to the selected region (US/EU/APAC) for active serving and persisted logs.
- Transient cross-region processing: supported for failover, analytics batch jobs, and cache rebuild tasks. We currently allow transient hops for up to 48 hours in standard SLA; longer windows require a contractual exception.
- Notification SLA: we can commit to proactive email + console alert 2 hours prior to scheduled non-emergency cross-region egress; emergency failovers will be notified within 1 hour of action.
- Subprocessors: we will provide a roster export with activation timestamps and RSS-of-change; see attached roster CSV.
- Evidence: we can produce a packet with redacted audit log slices (showing egress events), an example alert from Console, and a short playbook describing keys and escrow options.

Questions from our side to align the MAP:
1) Do you require customer-managed KMS for all keys (we offer optional CMK + escrow) or is an attestation sufficient?
2) For analytics/batch work, are you OK with a scheduled maintenance window (agreeable times) versus on-demand runs?
3) Is there a maximum acceptable transient window (you mentioned 72h during call)? We noted 48h is our standard.

I’m looping Marissa for DPA/legal redlines and Rishi for the operational evidence bundle. I’ll prepare a 1-page MAP with timelines once you confirm the CMK preference and the target window.

—
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@healthlyte.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-05T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask: geo commitments + subprocessor roster

Tom / Tessa — I’ve uploaded a DPA with our suggested redlines (attached: Healthlyte_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf). High level notes:
- We accept a binding commitment to region pinning for customer production data as described, with a documented temporary failover carveout.
- We’ll add language that transient cross-region processing will not exceed 48 hours unless an exception is approved by both parties; if you need 72 hours we can discuss an escalation path with legal.
- For KMS: we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS). If you choose CMK, we can provide optional escrow of wrapped key material for emergency restore; escrow access is limited and audited.

Attached is our current subprocessor roster export (subprocessors_roster_20270503.csv) — it includes vendor name, role, data types processed, and activation timestamp. We can also produce an audit sample showing subprocessor activation events in the Console (redacted).

DocuSign link (pre-filled) is here: https://www.docusign.com/verify?envelopeId=0a1b2c3d4e — please review the redlines and add any comments, we’ll iterate quickly.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: Healthlyte_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf, subprocessors_roster_20270503.csv
From: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@healthlyte.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Healthlyte Legal <legal@healthlyte.com>, healthlyte-procurement@healthlyte.com
Date: 2027-05-05T10:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask: geo commitments + subprocessor roster

Thanks Marissa — a few follow-ups from legal and our InfoSec team:
- Can you produce a short (1-2 page) evidence packet showing an actual transient failover event (audit log slice + timestamp + subprocessor activation) redacted for customer identifiers? We need this for our auditors.
- We need the notification SLA to include at least one out-of-band channel (email + webhook) to our security mailbox. Can you confirm support for a webhook callback and the payload sample?
- Emergency failover: subject to escrow access timeline — if escrow is used, what are the authorization gates and typical time-to-access? Our lawyers want a measured upper bound.
- Regarding the window: Healthlyte can accept 48 hours for routine transient windows; for critical DR tests we may ask for a temporary 72-hour window but that must be scheduled in advance and limited to a named activation.

On the operational side, please include a sample alert email format in the packet — that will speed sign-off. Attaching legal@healthlyte.com to keep them in the loop.

Best,
Tom

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@healthlyte.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-06T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Geo-commitment, DPA redlines, and operational evidence request — MAP + evidence bundle

Tom / team — attaching the operational MAP (inline below and attachment: transient-egress-playbook_20270504.pdf). Key commitments and timeline:

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — Healthlyte / Redwood
- Day 0 (today): Confirm KMS choice (Redwood-managed vs CMK). Healthlyte to reply with selection.
- Day 1: Redwood provides evidence packet: (1) redacted audit log slice showing a transient egress event, (2) sample alert email + webhook payload schema, (3) subprocessor activation timeline CSV.
- Day 2: Legal parties sign DPA redlines via DocuSign; Redwood will accept a single minor amendment for a scheduled 72-hour test window to be mutually agreed.
- Day 3: Ops-runbook and playbook delivered to Healthlyte Secure Confluence link; scheduled walkthrough (30 min) with Healthlyte InfoSec.

Operational commitments (specifics):
- Transient window: standard 48 hours for unscheduled failover; scheduled test windows up to 72 hours by mutual agreement.
- Notification: email + console alert + webhook to the URL you provide; proactive notice 2 hours prior for scheduled events and within 1 hour for emergency failovers.
- KMS/Escrow: if CMK chosen, escrow wrapped key material is stored in HSM-backed escrow; access requires two-person approval (Redwood legal + Healthlyte security designee) and is logged and audited. Typical time-to-access (non-blocked) is 4–6 hours; for emergency pre-authorized scenarios we can commit to 2 hours.
- Evidence: we will deliver a redacted audit slice and a CSV of subprocessor activation timestamps with each row keyed to the activation event ID (redacted IDs).

Next steps for you: confirm CMK choice and provide webhook endpoint + preferred contact for out-of-band security notifications. Once we have these we’ll push the evidence packet to the secured share and kick the DocuSign flow.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the packet.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Platform Security | Redwood Inference
attachments: transient-egress-playbook_20270504.pdf
